title: Unlearnable, or Unmeasured? On the Reliability of Difficulty Labels in RLVR
abstract: arXiv:2609.40115v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has become an important approach for improving reasoning during post-training. Recent work suggests that some difficult prompts remain resistant to learning even when they occasionally produce correct solutions. We revisit this unlearnability phenomenon and find that the affected prompts do improve, at roughly one third of the learnable rate, while the difficulty-defined set used to study them is much less reproducible than expected. These difficulty labels are estimated from a limited number of sampled responses. Combining them across seeds can further change which prompts are selected instead of simply reducing measurement noise. We develop a sampling-based framework for quantifying this instability and determining how much evaluation is required for difficulty assignments to reproduce reliably. translated_title: 不可学习，还是未被充分测量？论RLVR中难度标签的可靠性
translated_abstract: 带可验证奖励的强化学习（RLVR）已成为在后训练阶段提升推理能力的重要方法。近期研究表明，某些困难提示即使偶尔能产生正确的解答，也依然难以被学习。我们重新审视了这一“不可学习”现象，发现受影响的提示实际上确实在进步，其进步速率约为可学习提示的三分之一；而用于研究该现象的按难度定义的提示集合，其可复现性远低于预期。这些难度标签是从有限数量的采样响应中估计得到的，跨随机种子合并这些标签可能会进一步改变被选中的提示，而不仅仅是减少测量噪声。我们开发了一个基于采样的框架，用于量化这种不稳定性，并确定难度分配需要多少评估量才能可靠复现。我们还重新审视了为解释不可学习性而提出的梯度相似性证据……
tldr: 该研究发现RLVR中被认为“不可学习”的困难提示其实以约三分之一的可学习速率在改进，真正的问题在于基于有限采样估计的难度标签不可靠，作者据此提出了量化标签不稳定性及确定所需评估量的采样框架。
